findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT (RTE) FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

A food handler was observed to handled cooked RTE foods as they were moving them to cold holding/cooling. Education was conducted with the PIC and should be trickled down to staff moving forward. Tongs or gloves are needed to handle RTE foods that do not have another kill step prior to service. Ensure that all RTE foods are handled safely at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cooked steak was observed in a pan at 120F internal temperatures. The pan is attempting a double boiler style of hot holding but the edges of the pans do not meet. This is allowing the hot air and steam to escape as apposed to being trapped and transferring the heat to the TCS foods. The procedures in place are not allowing for effective hot holding of the foods. Per the PIC the steak was prepared at noon and placed in the hot holding at that time. This puts the four hour limit for foods being out of temperature at 4 pm that afternoon. The PIC was instructed to discard the foods at that time, and they did. A new situation for the hot holding of these foods will need to be put in place moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

A mop was observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mop so that it would drip/air dry effectively. Ensure that the mops are stored so that they effectively dry each time in the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:

(B) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section.

6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

findings.comment:

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Beans cooling in the freezer were probed to be 103°F (p). PIC stated that beans began cooling 1.5 hours. Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. CORRECTED- Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Additional efforts were made to cool food within the 2 hour time frame.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
An opened gallon of whole milk in the Rockstar cooler is not marked with an in-house use-by date. CORRECTED- Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was labeled with the date it was opened. 
3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

Soup, enchilada sauce, and salsa exceed the time limit. Foods were dated 12-26-19 and 1-5-20. CORRECTED- Food was discarded. Ensure foods are not held longer than 7 days after preparation or opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Large cuts of meat were observed thawing at room temperature in a non-functioning walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Meat was observed to be 28°F, and was relocated to the functioning walk-in cooler to complete thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.
